{{Recipe}}

'''Chinese five spice powder''' (五香粉, '''five spices powder,''' or '''five-spice powder''') is a convenient seasoning for Cantonese cuisine. It incorporates the five basic flavours of Chinese cooking—sweet, sour, bitter, pungent, and salty. One common recipe includes China Tung Hing cinnamon, powdered [[Cookbook:Cassia|cassia]] buds, powdered [[Cookbook:Star Anise|star anise]] and [[Cookbook:Anise|anise]] seed, [[Cookbook:Ginger|ginger root]], and ground [[Cookbook:Clove|clove]]s. Another recipe for the powder consists of [[Cookbook:Cinnamon|cinnamon]], [[Cookbook:Pepper|black pepper]], cloves, [[Cookbook:Fennel|fennel]] seed, and star anise. It is used in most Cantonese roasted [[Cookbook:Duck|ducks]], as well as [[Cookbook:Beef|beef]] stew. Although this spice is used in restaurant cooking, many Chinese households never use it in day-to-day cooking.

The formulae are based on the Chinese philosophy of balancing the yin and yang in food. A pinch of the powder goes a long way. A versatile seasoned salt can be easily made by stir-frying common [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]] with five spice powder under low heat in a dry pan until the spice and salt are well mixed.

== Ingredients ==
* 2 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|teaspoons]] [[Cookbook:Szechuan Pepper|Szechuan peppercorns]]
* 8 [[Cookbook:Star Anise|star anise]] pods
* ½ [[Cookbook:Tsp|tsp]] ground [[Cookbook:Clove|cloves]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tablespoon]] ground [[Cookbook:Cinnamon|cinnamon]]
* 1 tablespoon ground [[Cookbook:Fennel|fennel]] seeds

== Procedure ==
#Toast the Szechuan peppercorns in a dry frying pan for about 3 minutes.
#Grind the peppercorns in a pepper grinder or coffee grinder together with the star anise pods.
#[[Cookbook:Sifting|Sift]] the ground spices to remove any larger bits.
#Mix together the cloves, cinnamon, and fennel seeds.
#Grind the completed mixture until it is a very fine powder.
#Use sparingly, as it is extremely pungent.
